why: False contrast: denies something nobody claimed.
replacement: State the second half directly and add the specific fact.
example_before: This isn't about tools. It's about people.
example_after: The team needs two days of training; licences cost less.

why: Chat formula left in the text; the first words alone often reveal the model [Sun 2025].
replacement: Delete it and start with the content.
example_before: Certainly! Here is a summary of the meeting.
example_after: The meeting agreed on a March launch.

regex: \bas an ai( language model)?\b|\bi hope this helps\b|\blet me know if you (need|have|want) anything else\b|\bfeel free to (ask|reach out)\b
why: Assistant boilerplate.
replacement: Delete it; end with the last concrete point.
example_after: The template is attached.

why: Filler opener.
replacement: Start with the claim.
example_before: In today's fast-paced world, time is scarce.
example_after: We have twenty minutes for the review.

regex: \b(did you know|have you ever wondered|what if i told you)\b
why: Rhetorical opener.
replacement: Start with the fact itself.
example_before: Did you know most invoices are paid late?
example_after: Our clients pay 40 % of invoices after the due date.

why: Announces content instead of giving it.
replacement: Start with the first point.
example_after: First, the pricing.

regex: \bthe (harsh|hard|ugly|uncomfortable) truth is\b|\blet'?s be (real|honest)\b|\bhere'?s the thing\b|\blet that sink in\b|\bread that again\b
why: Fake tension.
replacement: Say the point plainly.
example_before: Here's the thing: nobody reads it.
example_after: Only 18 % of visitors finish the article.

why: Addresses everyone and no one.
replacement: Name one specific reader.
example_before: Whether you're a founder or a freelancer…
example_after: For agencies with more than ten clients.

why: False contrast „It's not just X, it's Y“.
replacement: State what it actually does.
example_before: It's not just an app, it's a lifestyle.
example_after: The app tracks protein and reminds you to eat.

why: Question and one-word answer on cue.
replacement: Write one sentence with the reason.
example_after: It paid back in three months.

regex: \bgame[- ]?changer\w*\b|\b(take|taking|takes) (it|your \w+|things) to the next level\b|\blike never before\b|\bthe power of\b
why: Marketing cliché.
replacement: Say what concretely improves and by how much.
example_after: Orders now ship in one day instead of two.

why: Hype verb.
replacement: Say what the reader gets.
example_after: You will close the books two days earlier.

why: LinkedIn template.
replacement: Say the news and why it matters.
example_before: I'm thrilled to announce our new feature!
example_after: We launched invoice import from Xero.

regex: \bstay tuned\b|\bwhat are your thoughts\?|\blet me know in the comments\b
why: Generic sign-off.
replacement: Ask one concrete question or end with the last point.
example_after: The next release ships on 4 March.

regex: \bi hope (this|my) (e-?mail|message) finds you well\b|\bi hope you'?re (doing )?well\b|\bi hope you (are|have) (doing well|had a great)\b
why: Email filler opener.
replacement: Go straight to the reason for writing.
example_before: I hope this email finds you well.
example_after: I'm sending the offer for Tuesday's meeting.

regex: \b(i )?(just )?wanted to (reach out|touch base|follow up|circle back)\b|\bcircle back\b|\btouch base\b
why: Corporate filler.
replacement: Say what you need and by when.
example_before: I wanted to circle back on this.
example_after: Can you confirm the price by Friday?

regex: \b(please )?(do not|don'?t) hesitate to (contact|reach out|ask)\b|\bshould you have any (questions|concerns)\b
why: Template call to action.
replacement: Give one concrete next step.
example_before: Please don't hesitate to reach out.
example_after: Call me on Thursday after 2 pm if the date doesn't work.

why: Offer buzzword without proof.
replacement: Replace with a fact: a number, a client type, a result.
example_after: We set up invoice import for accounting firms in two days.

why: Feedback sandwich: the praise is a wrapper, not information.
replacement: Name what works specifically, then the issue and the fix.
example_before: Great job overall, but the intro is weak.
example_after: The pricing table is clear. The intro needs the client's problem in the first sentence.

regex: \bit (might|may|could) be worth (considering|exploring|thinking about)\b|\byou (might|may) want to consider\b
why: Over-cushioned criticism hides the point.
replacement: Say what to change and why.
example_before: It might be worth considering a shorter intro.
example_after: Cut the intro to two sentences; the offer starts too late.

why: Czech calque of „na druhé straně“; English says „on the other hand“.
replacement: on the other hand
example_before: On the other side, it is cheaper.
example_after: On the other hand, it is cheaper.

regex: \bin the frame of\b|\bon the base of\b|\bon (a )?(daily|weekly|monthly) base\b
why: Czech calque („v rámci“, „na základě“, „na denní bázi“).
replacement: within / as part of / based on / daily
example_before: In the frame of the project we tested it.
example_after: As part of the project, we tested it.

regex: \bit is (necessary|needed) to say that\b|\bwe can say that\b
why: Throat-clearing meta phrase, common in Czech-English („je nutné říct“, „dá se říct“).
replacement: Just say it.
example_before: It is necessary to say that prices rose.
example_after: Prices rose.

why: False friend: „aktuální“ means current, „actual“ means real.
replacement: current (if you mean aktuální)
example_before: Please send me the actual price list.
example_after: Please send me the current price list.

why: Czech email calque („v příloze“, „s pozdravem“).

example_before: In the attachment you find the offer.
example_after: The offer is attached.

why: Czech calque („udělat fotku“, „kontrolovat“ in the sense of check).

why: Padding when there is no real contrast.
